newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: SOCCER-MARADONA SPENDS "SADDEST BIRTHDAY" DEFENDING MANAGER.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MARADONA SPENDS "SADDEST BIRTHDAY" DEFENDING MANAGER.

text.p: Argentina's fallen soccer idol Diego Maradona marked "the saddest birthday of his life" on Wednesday, promising never to abandon his manager and friend Guillermo Coppola who is in jail on cocaine-dealing charges.
"People have told me 'forget Guillermo' but I won't ever forget my friend," Maradona told local radio.

The captain of Argentina's 1986 World Cup-winning team chose his 36th birthday to turn out for training for Buenos Aires team Boca Juniors for the first time in months. He last played in mid-August, shortly before admitting his cocaine habit and committing himself to a Swiss drug clinic.
Maradona looked overweight but that did not stop the local media from speculating he would try for a place in Sunday's derby against Independiente.
Giving evidence on Tuesday, he corroborated Coppola's story that his manager knew nothing about the pound (400 grams) of cocaine police found in a flower pot in his Buenos Aires apartment.

The 49-year-old playboy, charged with possession of drugs for sale, could face up to 20 years in jail. He says the drugs were planted at his home after he left, by one of three women who stayed there with Maradona at a party days before the raid.

"This is the saddest birthday of my life," Maradona said. "I want my friend out of jail. He's no saint but he's not as bad as they make him out. What is Guillermo? The most pathetic drug trafficker in the world?" Maradona insisted there were "no drugs" at the party, just champagne and card games.

His brother-in-law, Gabriel Esposito, and former soccer international Alberto Tarantini were also arrested. Natalia de Negri, Tarantini's girlfriend, has been accused by two other women of putting the cocaine in the flower pot.
The case has evolved into a soap opera, with members of the jet set and girlfriends half their age parading through television studios with lurid tales of drugs and prostitution.
Two women witnesses have admitted to "intimate relations" with the undercover policemen who arrested Coppola while the judge and Coppola's lawyer call each other names on television.
De Negri has accused Coppola's attorney of threatening her and bribing two women $100,000 to say she planted the drugs.
The case is embarrassing President Carlos Menem, who backs the death penalty for drug smugglers. Coppola was a friend of his late son, Carlitos, and his private secretary, Ramon Hernandez.

Maradona talks of "dark political and economic interests" behind Coppola's arrest. But many blame Coppola for Maradona's drug habit which has earned him bans and charges of switched urine samples after a routine post-match drug test.
